title: Week of September 21, 2026
summary: Fall arrives Tuesday night as the coast settles into shoulder season: hawks are moving over Cape Henlopen, Grove Park's market keeps going, and James Farm is this week's free Hidden Gem near Bethany. Looking ahead, The Point's bayside beach reopens Oct. 1, the Lewes market shifts to its fall home, and October's festival calendar starts filling fast.

dailySlots.headline: The coast exhales: equinox, hawks on the move, and October taking shape
dailySlots.note: This is a transition week rather than a giant-event week. Fall arrives Tuesday night; Grove Park's farmers market runs Tuesday; the Cape Henlopen hawk watch is in fall migration season; and The Point's bayside beach is on track to reopen Oct. 1. Further out, the Rehoboth Beach Jazz Festival and Sea Witch are worth planning around now.

dailySlots.headline: Fall arrives at 8:05 p.m. tonight
dailySlots.note: The September equinox lands at 8:05 p.m. EDT tonight (00:05 UTC Sept. 23). On the Delaware coast, it is less a hard switch than a marker: crowds are thinner, the water still carries summer warmth, and shoulder season is underway.

dailySlots.headline: Raptors are streaming past the old WWII bunker at Cape Henlopen
dailySlots.note: Delaware's Hawk Watch program has counted fall migration from Cape Henlopen since 1995, using a platform atop a historic World War II bunker. Migration runs roughly mid-August through December, with counters generally on site from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., weather permitting.

dailySlots.headline: How Delaware went from 'invisible territory' to a state, told in maps
dailySlots.note: The Rehoboth Beach Museum currently lists 'Emerging Delaware: Maps from the Preston Schell Collection, 1628–1868' in its Upper Gallery. The exhibition traces colonial claims, boundary disputes and Delaware's emergence as a separate political identity through historic maps.

dailySlots.headline: Three miles of marsh-to-forest trail near Bethany, and free
dailySlots.note: James Farm Ecological Preserve in Ocean View is open sunrise to sundown year-round at no charge. Its 150 acres include more than three miles of marked trails, seven distinct habitats, three observation platforms and a boardwalk beach crossing.

dailySlots.headline: Black sea bass rules changed for 2026 — and state and federal waters now match
dailySlots.note: DNREC says NOAA aligned federal waters with Delaware's revised 2026–27 rules before the season opened: 12.5-inch minimum, 15 fish per person, and an open season from May 1 through Dec. 31 with no Oct. 1–9 closure. Regulations can change, so check DNREC's current fishing rules before keeping fish.
